inline_comments.comment: The snippet correctly includes `'**/**.tsx'` alongside the custom workspace path, but there is no inline comment explaining *why* both are required. When a user explicitly sets `include`, it replaces the default (`['**/**.tsx']`) entirely — omitting the first entry would mean only workspace files are scanned and the user's own project TSX files would no longer be covered by react-docgen-typescript. A developer reading this snippet could reasonably interpret `'**/**.tsx'` as boilerplate and delete it. Consider adding an inline comment such as `// Keep the default pattern to preserve coverage of your own project's files` immediately before the first array entry.

The `include` array mixes two different glob styles on the same line: `'**/**.tsx'` (non-standard double-wildcard before the extension) and `'../../packages/ui/src/**/*.tsx'` (conventional `**/*.tsx`). In most glob implementations these are functionally equivalent, but the visual inconsistency within the same array is likely to confuse readers. If `**/**.tsx` is intentionally preserved to match the plugin's internal default exactly, a brief inline comment explaining that would prevent confusion. Otherwise, using `**/*.tsx` consistently across both entries is cleaner and more idiomatic.

The opening paragraph and the section heading make no mention of Vite-based frameworks, yet the root-cause explanation on the next paragraph is entirely Vite-specific (`@joshwooding/vite-plugin-react-docgen-typescript`). Developers using Webpack-based Storybook frameworks (which use `react-docgen-typescript-plugin` instead) may read this section, attempt the same `include` fix, and find it unhelpful or differently structured. Scoping the section early — for example, updating the heading to "Inherited props are missing for components from workspace packages (Vite)" or adding a leading note like "This applies to Vite-based frameworks" — would prevent confusion and wasted effort for Webpack users.

The closing sentence — "Note that `tsconfigPath` only affects compiler options — it does not change which files are included in the TypeScript program." — is appended to the adjustment note without a clear logical bridge. It reads as an afterthought rather than an integrated part of the explanation. Consider either (a) moving it into the root-cause paragraph where the `include` glob behavior is first described, or (b) surfacing it as a distinct callout/admonition block so it's visually distinct and more discoverable for readers who are currently trying `tsconfigPath` as their fix.

general_comments.comment: The new snippet file only provides TypeScript (`language="ts"`) variants for both the CSF 3 and CSF Next tabs. Other configuration snippets in the project (e.g., `main-config-typescript-react-docgen-typescript-options.md`) include JavaScript language variants as well. Since a user configuring `reactDocgenTypescriptOptions` in a JS-based `.storybook/main.js` would benefit from a JS example, consider adding JS variants for completeness, consistent with the project's established pattern.

The example workspace path `../../packages/ui/src/**/*.tsx` assumes a specific monorepo layout (exactly two directories up, with a `packages/ui/src/` structure). While the prose says to "Adjust the path to match your monorepo layout," the highly concrete example may anchor readers too strongly to that exact layout. Using a more deliberately generic placeholder — such as `../../<workspace-package>/src/**/*.tsx` or pointing to documentation on how to determine the correct relative path — would signal more clearly that this portion requires customization.
